examples.title: Calculate without inventing the recipe
examples.situation: A trainer-approved card eventually supplies three mass fractions c, p and b for a 5 kg tomato product.
reasoning: First check c+p+b=1 and confirm that all three materials are authorized and the P need is evidenced.
Then calculate masses as 5c, 5p and 5b kg; add them to verify 5 kg before weighing.
If the card gives volume parts instead, do not put those fractions straight onto a scale; obtain bulk-density and moisture instructions.
examples.takeaway: Actual numeric ingredient masses remain pending the documented trainer card.

examples.title: Do not transfer the clay example
examples.situation: A teacher model shows an outdoor 50:50 raised bed, while a bank process card says roughly 1 part compost to 2 parts clay in a container and another card asks for a 5 kg tomato blend.
reasoning: Three different purposes, with potentially different mass/volume bases, site material and water behaviour.
Retain 50:50 as the outdoor source example and approximately 1:2 as the separate process-card example, but do not apply either as the 5 kg tomato recipe.
Ask the trainer for the approved specification and tests for each real task.
examples.takeaway: No universal proportion follows from the three cards.
